web_sources.title: PSTRAPS: straps readout and override
web_sources.relevant_quote: Straps sampled on reset from pull-up/pull-down resistors placed by board manufacturer. Set1 bit4: PCI device class — 0: 0x030200 [3d controller], 1: 0x030000 [vga controller]. PSTRAPS MMIO at 0x101000-0x101FFF [NV3+] BAR0. bit31 STRAPSx_PRIMARY = override enable. Set0 bits 10-13/28/30 = DEVICE_ID bits (G80+).
web_sources.applicability_tu106: MECHANISM ONLY — EnvyTools covers NV1:GF119/G80+ families; NO TU106 pin-to-bit mapping. Every TU106 strap-to-class mapping is EXTRAPOLATION.
web_sources.next_discriminator: Find TU106-specific devinit/VBIOS strap table or read PSTRAPS register read-only

web_sources.title: GPU chips (envytools gpu.rst)
web_sources.relevant_quote: Turing family: TU102, TU104, TU106, TU116, TU117. TU106 pciid 1f0X# (device IDs 0x1F0X choosable by straps). Last few bits [0-6 depending on GPU] of PCI device id are changeable through straps.
web_sources.applicability_tu106: TU106 device ID range documented; confirms device ID can be strap-selected but gives no per-value strap map.
web_sources.next_discriminator: Compare VBIOS strap tables between 0x1F0B (CMP) and 0x1F06/0x1F02 (GeForce) ROMs

web_sources.title: TU116 strap mod: Basic Display Adapter, Device ID unchanged
web_sources.relevant_quote: Strap mod on TU116/CMP 30HX → system reports 'Microsoft Basic Display Adapter', Device ID stays 21C9 (not 21C4).
web_sources.applicability_tu106: TU116 — transfer gap; evidence that ID may be fuse/firmware-locked, not freely strap-selectable.
web_sources.next_discriminator: Read original issue if detail needed
